text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 3.2 million shillings of Uganda coffee destined for London, is recovered in a Nairobi businessman's yard.
- A go-slow at the Kilindini Harbour in Mombasa causes congestion of container ships which are unable to berth due to a delay in offloading cargo.
- A 61-year-old man denies raping two sisters, saying he does not have the strength to engage in sexual intercourse.
- A Kenyan court orders that ailing political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere be taken for dental examination and eye tests.
- The Pan African Insurance Company stands to lose over 22 million shillings following the collapse of Kenya Finance Bank.
- The Raila Odinga FORD-Kenya faction mounts pressure on rival FORD-Kenya camp to speed up the process of fresh party polls as ordered by the high court recently.
- Members of the public accuse private banks with a majority of foreign shareholding of flouting the Cheques Act and making billions from charges imposed on the customers, illegally.
